Items.Authors: In-Ung Song, Chang-Jin Oh, Andrew E. Lowman, Jamison C. Noenickx, Sukmock Lee, Connie Rockosi, Tim Miller
Items.Title: Conceptual design of wavefront sensing for the Spec-S5 large wide field segmented telescope
Items.Abstract: This study employs dispersed fringe sensors (DFS) and a phase retrieval (PR) scheme to co-phase the primary mirror segments and assess system performance of the Spec-S5 telescope. DFS measures relative piston values between adjacent segments to align the eight primary mirror segments, while PR detects fine-scale wavefront errors using multiple image sensors positioned at the center and edges of the image plane. These sensors enable single-shot measurements through a custom octagonal wedged Grism and field diversity concept. Validation on a test bench with a commercial telescope confirmed performance better than 100 nm RMS, demonstrating the suitability of DFS and PR for Spec-S5.

Items.Authors: Silvia Regalado Olivares, María Jesús Martínez González, Patricia Gómez González, Carlos Quintero Noda, Jonai Bienes Pérez, Antonio Matta-Gómez
Items.Title: Conceptual optical design of EMBER, the infrared integral field spectropolarimeter for EST
Items.Abstract: EMBER is the infrared integral field spectropolarimeter for the European Solar Telescope (EST). The instrument is a high-resolution spectrograph that will cover the solar spectrum from 1 to 2.2 μm and is optimised for 1.083 μm. In addition, it will provide spectropolarimetric observations using a dual-beam configuration. The spectrograph follows a Czerny-Turner design and will observe a 2D input field of view (FoV) of 10” x 10”. This wide FoV will be reorganised by a slicer mirror-based Integral Field Unit (IFU) that is composed by 400 slicers. The IFU output is subsequently rearranged into 10 slits that feed the spectrograph. This work presents the current status of the conceptual optical design of EMBER.

Items.Authors: Peter Spanoudakis, Mathias Gumy, Yves-Julien Regamey, Cyril Rupf, Juan Lahera Perez, Jonathan Bennès, Philippe Schwab, Stéphane Humbert
Items.Title: Configurable Slit Unit development for the MIRMOS (Multi-Object Spectrometer for Infra-Red Exploration) instrument for the Magellan telescope
Items.Abstract: The MIRMOS instrument will integrate a reconfigurable slit mask unit (CSU) which is a mechanism allowing to generate a multi-slit configuration at the focal plane of the telescope. The CSU creates slits on the focal plane by displacing two opposing bars with the space between them creating a slit and allowing light of a selected object to be transmitted to the detector. The mechanism is being developed for the Multi-Object Spectrometer for Infra-Red Exploration (MIRMOS) instrument to be installed on one of the two 6.5m Magellan telescopes at the Las Campanas Observatory in Chile. MIRMOS will provide NIR multi-object spectroscopy over a field of view of 3' x 13'. The reconfigurable mask allows the formation of 92 optical slits in a 66 x 266 mm2 field of view. The mechanism is a derivative design from the successful MOSFIRE CSU in operation on the Keck Observatory since 2012.

Items.Authors: Jared A. Termini, Keri Hoadley, Casey DeRoo, Cecilia R. Fasano, Fernando Cruz Aguirre, Paul Scowen, Manuel Quijada, Mateo Batkis, Luis Rodriguez de Marcos, Javier Del Hoyo, Gavin Frueh
Items.Title: Connecting the fabrication quality and UV performance of gratings to predict the UV performance of large-format gratings
Items.Abstract: UV spectroscopy is a powerful tool for probing astrophysical systems, as it traces baryonic matter across many phases and temperatures. Achieving our future science goals will require high-performance, large-format gratings, but directly measuring their UV efficiency is costly and time-consuming. If trends between the UV performance and fabrication quality of small gratings can predict the performance of larger gratings, we can streamline the UV grating characterization process.    We present results from a multi-year study assessing fabrication quality and UV performance of small gratings. We use optical interferometry to determine the gratings’ period error and limiting resolution. We use single-point metrology to measure the surface roughness. We characterize the gratings’ UV performance via efficiency measurements from 900-2000Å. We investigate correlations between fabrication metrics and UV performance, enabling metrology-based prediction of large-format grating performance.

Items.Authors: Travis Curtis, Oswald H. W. Siegmund, Jason B. McPhate, Bennet Schwab, Andrew Ji
Items.Title: Continued progress towards a large-format, hermetically sealed, high-resolution UV MCP detector
Items.Abstract: We report continued progress on a large-format, high-resolution ultraviolet (UV) detector. The 10 × 10 cm² device is a hermetically sealed microchannel plate (MCP) detector. It consists of a proximity-focused, UV-transmissive fused silica window, atomic layer deposited (ALD) MCPs, an opaque alkali-halide photocathode, and a high-temperature co-fired ceramic (HTCC) cross-strip (XS) anode. The device design, assembly, and integration activities are discussed, along with preliminary performance results.  This work represents a step forward in addressing critical astrophysics technology gap priorities related to large-format, high-resolution UV detector technology. It advances capabilities required for a future strategic missions and could be suitable for a range of smaller programs in the near term.

Items.Authors: Mate Adamkovics
Items.Title: Coupling light into photonic circuit waveguides with micro-optics for scientific instrumentation
Items.Abstract: Instruments that incorporate integrated photonics can be designed to decrease size, improve stability, and implement novel functionality. Photonic technologies such as couplers/splitters, arrayed waveguide gratings, resonators, and modulators, can be used measure the information that is collected by telescopes in ways that are not possible with traditional optics. One specific application is the photonic coronagraph, which provides particularly high contrast using interferometric nulling. A critical challenge for using photonic devices in astronomical instruments is the coupling efficiently from free-space into the waveguides of the photonic integrated circuit (PIC). Grating couplers are one of the most common interfaces, yet they achieve a peak efficiency over a narrow spectral bandpass. We present our work on 3d-printed micro-optics for efficient wide-band coupling into PIC waveguides and discuss how efficient coupling into PICs can enable future space telescopes.

Items.Authors: Nicholas MacDonald, William Deich, Daren Dillon, Michael Gonzales, Renate Kupke, Dale Sandford, Andy Skemer, Deno Stelter
Items.Title: Cryogenic lenslet array and mode-selecting mechanism for SCALES: design, fabrication, and performance testing
Items.Abstract: The SCALES instrument, scheduled for deployment in 2026 on the Keck II telescope, employs a silicon lenslet array to divide the incoming focal plane into discrete spatial elements (spaxels) for integral-field spectroscopy of planetary systems. The array enables two observational modes: a low-resolution mode (R ~ 60) operating from 2–5 µm, and a medium-resolution mode (R ~ 2000) covering the same spectral range. Mode selection is achieved through a combination of a mode-blocking shutter upstream of the lenslet array and a two-position mechanism downstream that inserts a return mirror for the medium-resolution optical path. This paper presents the design and fabrication of the silicon lenslet array, its isothermal mounting strategy within the cryogenic environment, and the associated opto-mechanical mechanisms that facilitate reliable mode switching. We describe the performance, operational behavior, and integration of these subsystems within the SCALES instrument architecture.

Items.Authors: Gerhard Ulbricht, Gary Donegan, Cáthal McAleer, Stephenie Brophy Lee, Mario De Lucia, Eoin Baldwin, Jack Piercy, Oisín Creaner, Piotr Wawer, Przemysław Nita, Deirdre Coffey, Tom Ray
Items.Title: Cryogenic qualification testing of dichroic filters 1-5 for ESA’s ARIEL mission
Items.Abstract: ARIEL, the Atmospheric Remote‐sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large‐survey mission, is ESA’s Cosmic Vision M4 mission and will study the atmospheres of up to 1000 exoplanets. It uses a set of five dichroic filters (D1 to D5) to split the incoming bandwidth of 0.5 to 7.8 μm and will operate between 40 K and 60 K. We will present ongoing efforts of qualification testing of the D1 - D5 dichroics. Our Tests are performed at ambient and cryogenic temperatures and include transmission and reflectivity spectra, the cryogenic shift of the dichroic’s transition wavelength, wave-front error measurements, humidity testing and cryogenic cycling between 37 K and 323 K. We will give a progress report and will elaborate on achieved results, experimental setups and encountered challenges. We will also discuss steps to establish an instrumentation clean room, suitable for flight acceptance testing for in-space instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Xianyi Zhou, Chuanxin Wei, Yonghe Chen, Jiaming Liang, Yanwu Kang, Yuji Zhu, Junfei Li
Items.Title: Cryogenic temperature compensation design for the optical structure of The Earth 2.0 (ET) Transit Telescope
Items.Abstract: This study addresses the thermal-structural matching challenge faced by the optical system of The Earth 2.0 (ET) Transit Telescope (comprising nine lenses with apertures of 276–344 mm) operating at –15 ℃. An optomechanical design integrating a two-stage flexible support structure with coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE)-matched materials is proposed, coupled with a low-temperature displacement pre-compensation method. By establishing a coupled thermal-structural-optical model, the predicted deformation is used as a feedforward correction in the alignment process to actively compensate for image quality drift under cryogenic conditions. The resulting system achieves an EE90 radius variation of less than 0.5 μm at –15 ℃, significantly enhancing on-orbit stability and providing a valuable reference for the development of similar cryogenic optical systems.

Items.Authors: Uwe D. Zeitner, Martin Heusinger, Thomas Flügel-Paul, Hans Dekker, Matteo Genoni
Items.Title: CUBES: grating design and manufacturing status
Items.Abstract: We report on the current state and intermediate results of the realization of the full-size diffraction gratings for the Cassegrain U-Band Efficient Spectrograph (CUBES) to be installed at ESO’s VLT. The CUBES design is based on two first-order transmission diffraction gratings of line density 3600 l/mm and 3112 l/mm, respectively. The gratings are optimized for peak diffraction efficiency of >95% in the wavelength bands 300…352nm and 346…405nm. Their realization is based on electron-beam lithography, a structure transfer into a fused silica substrate by reactive ion etching, and a fine-tuning of the grating structure by an Atomic-Layer-Deposition process.

Items.Authors: Sibo Van Gool, Bart Vandenbussche, Gert Raskin, Hugues Sana, Jan Goris, Pierre Royer, Maddalena Reggiani, Leonardo Peri, Julien Storm, Louis Storm
Items.Title: CubeSpec: development of the Payload Control Unit for a high-resolution spectroscopy CubeSat
Items.Abstract: The CubeSpec mission at KU Leuven brings optical spectroscopy to a 12U CubeSat platform to study massive stars, addressing the challenge of integrating advanced instrumentation in a compact, power-limited spacecraft. High pointing stability is achieved through three piezo actuators rotating a Fine Steering Mirror in closed-loop feedback with a Fine Guidance Sensor and actuator strain-gauge readings. The guidance and science detectors use GSENSE2020BSI CMOS sensors, each interfaced by an Artix-7 FPGA and streamed to a Zynq-7000–based payload processor. Additional components include high-voltage piezo drivers, an ADXL355 microvibration experiment, and CSP-based links for onboard communication and science data transfer.

Items.Authors: Taoran Li, Yan Wang, Lu Feng, Jianan Tao, Zhiyong Gao, Yong Zhao, Cheng Chen
Items.Title: Daytime thermal behavior of dome: Experiments and CFD simulation
Items.Abstract: Solar radiation directly heats the dome of an optical telescope during daytime, causing a rise in the temperature of the internal air and instruments, thereby deteriorating the dome seeing. To reduce the solar thermal load, the dome’s exterior surface has a high reflectivity coating and thermal insulation, blocking most of the radiation. This paper presents the measured reflectance of sample materials of the dome’s exterior surface, and the temperature-rise experiments under solar irradiation condition. We used a thermal imager and several temperature sensors to capture the instantaneous temperature and record the continuously temperature variation process. The measured data and the Computational Fluid Dynamics results show good consistency, verifying the reliability of the numerical model. This study provides essential material parameters and modeling foundations for thermal load simulations of large enclosure, offering guidance for the air condition systems design.

Items.Authors: Sydney Skorpen, Pradip Gatkine, Ian P. McLean, Jeremy Lin
Items.Title: Demonstration of an integrated R~30,000 astrophotonic spectrograph
Items.Abstract: By operating in the diffraction-limited regime, astrophotonic instruments break the scaling relationship between telescope and instrument sizes, unlocking increasingly high-resolution spectrographs in a compact, stable, and inexpensive format. Here, we present the results of integrating an R~30,000 chip-based arrayed waveguide grating (AWG) spectrograph sensitive to the NIR H-band (1.45-1.65 μm) in a packaged fiber-fed instrument, as well as on-sky testing. This assembly consists of the photonic spectrograph, followed by a cross-disperser to separate the spectral orders (each spanning ~12.5 nm waveband), and an InGaAs detector, all contained within a footprint equivalent to a shoebox. The package is made complete with a data-reduction pipeline that delivers wavelength-calibrated spectra. This pathfinder performance demonstration paves the way to mature facility-class photonic instruments, suitable for ground-based and space-based observatories.

Items.Authors: Jinyu Pan, Hangxin Ji, Ru Chen, Haoran Yu, Lili Wang, Jun Li, Yi Chen
Items.Title: Design and application of a balloon-borne ultraviolet spectrometer
Items.Abstract: This work reports a lightweight (＜10 kg) balloon-borne ultraviolet spectrometer engineered for continuous 200–400 nm measurements of key solar lines and atmospheric trace gases. Ground-based observations in this band are strongly attenuated, and current space missions lack full-band coverage. The instrument adopts a compact “slit–78 mm collimator–600 l/mm grating–105 mm imager–back-illuminated CMOS” layout, providing 1.2 nm FWHM spectral resolution within a 450×370×160 mm envelope. Atmospheric transmission from 5–22 km was modeled using MODTRAN 5 and validated with Py6S, yielding a dedicated near-UV transmittance database to guide system design and performance assessment. The prototype has completed opto-mechanical integration, and wavelength and flux calibrations are ongoing. A ≥22 km, ≥4 h high-altitude balloon flight is scheduled to verify in-situ optical performance, detector sensitivity, and system stability, supporting future extended-altitude UV remote-sensing missions.

Items.Authors: Andrzej S. Piascik
Items.Title: Design and characterisation of LIRIC: offsetting a compact infrared sCMOS detector within the image-plane
Items.Abstract: We present the design and characterisation of the Liverpool InfraRed Imaging Camera (LIRIC) deployed on the 2.0m Liverpool Telescope on La Palma in 2025.  LIRIC employs a science grade sCMOS InGaAs detector with a usable imaging area of 607 x 510 pixels, providing a 3.0 x 2.5 arcmin field-of-view.  Wavelength is selectable with J (1.1-1.4 µm) or H (1.5-1.7µm) via an integral filter wheel, which also has a gold mirror for darks.  The compact and lightweight design of the camera assembly allows for rapid repositioning to 17 fixed offsets within the focal plane using a simple cam mechanism.  This provides an alternative to offsetting the telescope or a tip-tilt mirror for generating sky background images subtraction.

Items.Authors: Thananphat Phonthongchanthuek, Pornapa Artsang, Pakakaew Rittipruk, Sirinrat Sithajan, Panomsak Meemon
Items.Title: Design and implementation of a dual-band Fourier Transform Spectrometer with multi-channel detection using off-the-shelf components
Items.Abstract: Fourier Transform Spectroscopy (FTS) provides high spectral resolution and broad spectral coverage, but extending operation from the near-UV to the NIR introduces challenges in beamsplitter performance and interferometric stability. This work presents an off-the-shelf dual-band FTS using a modified Michelson interferometer with three detection channels: visible, NIR, and metrology. Three optimized beamsplitters enable wide spectral coverage without custom optics while minimizing OPD errors. A frequency-stabilized He–Ne laser ensures precise OPD tracking and phase-distortion correction. Performance validation with 405 nm and 785 nm sources confirmed high fringe contrast and stable metrology. Broadband solar measurements further demonstrated clear astrophysical and telluric absorption features, verifying the system’s resolving power and spectral fidelity.

Items.Authors: Liurong Lin, Lucas Marquis, Ruben Tandon, Jonas G. Kühn
Items.Title: Design and implementation of a fast SLM-driven coherent differential imaging scheme for exoplanet high-contrast imaging
Items.Abstract: We present a fast SLM-based coherent differential imaging (CDI) framework designed to mitigate quasi-static and post-AO speckles that limit ground-based exoplanet imaging. Using synchronous zonal phase modulation in the focal-plane with an LCoS SLM, our approach distinguishes coherent speckles from astrophysical signals. Through simulations, we assess the impact of modulation parameters and astrophysical conditions on achievable contrast and inner working angle. With emerging low-noise high-speed NIR detectors, this time-domain CDI method may also address rapidly evolving post-AO residuals. We outline ongoing implementation efforts with a 400 Hz SLM paired with a C-RED One detector and describe plans for deployment as an upgrade to the PLACID instrument on the 4-m DAG telescope.

Items.Authors: Enrico Hilpert, Thomas Räthe, Eric Schmucker, Thomas Peschel, Peter Bizenberger, Harald Baumeister, Conchi Cárdenas Vázquez
Items.Title: Design and manufacturing of the METIS imager collimator system for ELT
Items.Abstract: The Metis Imager will be one of the first light instruments operating at Extremely Large Telescope. This talk will cover the design, simulation and manufacturing of the collimator system, one of three main optomechanical subsystems in the imager. Operating at a temperature of 40 K, the choice of materials is of crucial importance to retain mechanical and dimensional stability of the components. An all aluminum 6061 approach for metal mirrors and housing parts was selected to realize an athermal system. The presentation will give an overview of the manufacturing approach of the mirrors, including thermal stabilization, metrology and integration as well as the thermal and structural boundary conditions.

Items.Authors: Shuangquan Chen, Shuo Wang, Qihang Zhang, Zhen Zhang, Yonggang Gu, Chao Zhai
Items.Title: Design and optimization of the communication network for the new generation LAMOST fiber positioning system
Items.Abstract: To meet the urgent demand for 8,000 optical fiber positioning units of the new generation of LAMOST, this paper, based on the proposed double-layer CAN network architecture, completes the comprehensive upgrade and optimization of the communication network. The core work includes: upgrading the backbone of the entire network communication from the traditional CAN to CAN FD (covering the upper computer - intermediate node and intermediate node - child node), to solve the bandwidth bottleneck of large data volume; Redesign and optimize the communication hardware of the core hub center nodes in multiple versions; Establish an efficient and reliable three-level communication protocol. Experimental verification shows that the stability, throughput and real-time performance of the optimized communication network all meet the strict requirements of the system, providing key support for the efficient collaborative control of LAMOST's 8,000 optical fibers.

Items.Authors: Emma Rautio-Roe, Alexis Hill, Glen Herriot, Jeffrey Crane, Ross Cheriton, Zoran Ljusic, Thushara Gunaratne, Ralph Webber
Items.Title: Design and performance of a precision thermal system for the optical aperture synthesis laboratory demonstrator
Items.Abstract: The Optical Aperture Synthesis (OAS) laboratory demonstrator investigates the use of a photonic chip operating in closed loop with control electronics to sense and correct phase offsets between optical signals. This work helps validate the long‑term objective of coherently combining light from widely separated optical telescopes to enable extremely high‑resolution imaging and spectroscopy. To maintain phase synchronization within the correction range of the chip, the demonstrator’s thermal environment must meet stringent stability requirements. All phase‑sensitive components are housed in an actively controlled enclosure that has been fabricated and tested to maintain thermal stability within 10 milliKelvin. The thermal design also incorporates component‑specific temperature setpoints to ensure optimal operating conditions, minimizing noise and enhancing overall system performance.

Items.Authors: David B. Kieda
Items.Title: Design and performance of the Schwarzschild-Couder Telescope Camera for the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Schwarzschild-Couder Telescope (SCT) is a dual-mirror design proposed for the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) medium-energy range from 100 GeV to 10 TeV. The SCT offers a wide field of view of >8° and an imaging resolution of 0.067° using Silicon Photomultiplier (SiPM) photodetectors on the focal plane using 177 camera modules (64 SiPM pixels/module, 11,328 pixels total). A prototype SCT (pSCT), built and tested at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in southern Arizona, USA, used a partially populated camera with 25 modules (1600 pixels total). In this talk, we describe the design and performance of the full 11,328-pixel camera for the SCT telescope, which is being installed in 2026. Design improvements include upgraded SiPM and front-end electronics (FEE), improvements to camera motion control, cooling system, temperature control, and camera readout. The talk will describe the expected improvements in sensitivity resulting from the upgraded SCT camera.

Items.Authors: Pierre Noiré, Matthieu Cuq, Anthony L'Hostis, Thierry Roux
Items.Title: Design and qualification of custom hexapod positioning systems for optical alignment in extreme environments
Items.Abstract: This paper presents the influence of environmental constraints on the engineering design of hexapod positioning systems. These six-degree-of-freedom devices are widely used in telescope alignment and Ground Support Equipment (GSE) for optical alignment and qualification. Designers must contend with a range of challenging conditions, including vacuum, cleanroom, low temperatures, radiation, outdoor exposure, seismic activity,…  We present recent developments in custom positioners, highlighting the manufacturer’s expertise in meeting stringent environmental and operational requirements. This overview aims to share the current state of the art in engineering practices for advanced positioning systems, with a focus on the technical challenges posed by demanding environmental conditions.

Items.Authors: Bennet Schwab, Travis Curtis, Oswald Siegmund, Jason McPhate, Anton Tremsin
Items.Title: Design and test results of 50mm microchannel plate sealed tube detector for UV sounding rocket mission
Items.Abstract: New developments are presented on sealed tube microchannel plate detectors for two sounding rocket missions. This sensor is a hermetically sealed planacon tube with a proximity focused fused silica window and semitransparent bialkali photocathode. It combines a pair of 10-micron pore, 60:1 L/d, MgO Atomic Layer Deposited borosilicate microchannel plates with a high-resolution cross-strip anode. A novel external board converts the output of the cross strip anode into a cross delay line anode, simplifying the detectors on-board electrical interface while achieving the mission’s science-based performance requirements. This configuration is tailored for high efficiency imaging of far- and lyman-ultraviolet wavelengths with high resolution and low noise. Current testing meets the performance requirements of better than 100-micron spatial resolution. This detector will fly as part of two sounding rocket missions called FLUID and MOBIUS at the Laboratory of Atmospheric and Space Physics.

Items.Authors: Diane Chapuis Kerouanton, Gloria Mellinand, Malak Galal, Axel Nicolier, Aurélien Genin, Sébastien Pernecker, Rémi Giroud, Alexandre Jeanneau, Florence Laurent, Johan Richard, Jean-Paul Kneib
Items.Title: Design and testing of the motorized 2-DoF folding mirror 1 for the VLT BlueMUSE instrument
Items.Abstract: BlueMUSE is a blue-optimized, medium spectral resolution, panoramic integral field spectrograph under development for the Very Large Telescope (VLT). The project is now fully entering design phase. With an optimized transmission down to 350 nm, spectral resolution of R~3500 on average across the wavelength range, and a large FoV (1 arcmin²), BlueMUSE will open up a new range of galactic and extragalactic science cases facilitated by its specific capabilities.  In this paper, we present the design, implementation and evaluation of the motorized mount developed for Folding Mirror 1 (FM1) of the VLT BlueMUSE instrument. The mount provides two degrees of freedom in tip and tilt and is engineered to correct misalignments caused by environmental variations. The preliminary results demonstrate that the motorized FM1 tilt mount achieves the required precision and maintains alignment stability within the tight tolerances defined by the BlueMUSE project.

Items.Authors: Alicia M. Anderson, Samantha J. Thompson, Eugene B. Seneta, Alireza Esmaeilzadeh, Clark E. Baker, John S. Young
Items.Title: Design and verification of the HARPS3 exposure meter: a dual-band photometer for improved photon-weighted barycentric corrections
Items.Abstract: The High Accuracy Radial velocity Planet Searcher – 3 (HARPS3) is being developed for the Terra Hunting Experiment, a 10-year program targeting nightly observations of solar-like stars to search for long-period, low-mass exoplanets. Achieving 10 cm s⁻¹ radial-velocity precision requires accurate barycentric corrections, which depend on the true photon-weighted time of observation. Long exposures and CCD readout constraints make this difficult, so real-time flux monitoring is needed. Because atmospheric transmission varies across the optical range, the photon-weighted mid-time can differ for blue and red wavelengths. To account for this, we have designed a dual-band exposure meter for HARPS3 using a 550 nm dichroic to measure blue and red flux independently. We present the design, laboratory verification, and on-sky performance of this new system and compare it with the previous single-channel design.

Items.Authors: Hangxin Ji, Xiaoyu Pan, Haoran Yu, Zhen Tang, Lei Wang, Jinhu Lv, Jun Li
Items.Title: Design considerations and trade-offs for a high-efficiency UV-extended high-resolution polarimetric spectrograph for MOST
Items.Abstract: The MOST Telescope is a new-generation optical facility designed for remote and robotic operations, time-domain astronomy. To fully exploit its scientific potential, a high-resolution, high-efficiency stellar spectropolarimeter is under developing, enabling precise magnetic-field measurements and time-resolved polarimetry, and providing complementary coverage to ESPaDOnS and NARVAL. The instrument includes 340-1050nm spectral coverage, R~77,000, high UV throughput and instrumental stability. A comprehensive optical trade-off study was performed, examining image-slicer, main/cross-dispersion combination, and camera/CCD matching. Despite potential benefits, image slicers were rejected due to UV losses and system complexity. The final design adopts a mosaic R2.9 echelle, prism cross-disperser, and an F/2.5 UV-optimized camera matched to a deep depletion 4K CCD. This paper presents the design considerations, key trade-offs, and the anticipated performance of the MOST spectropolarimeter.

Items.Authors: Yi Meng, Hong-fei Zhang, Zong-wu He, Shi-hao Lu, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Design of a low-jitter pulse delay generator for astronomical gated cameras
Items.Abstract: Gated cameras are widely used in high temporal resolution observations of astronomy fields such as high resolution imaging of celestial bodies and laser guide star applications. To achieve precise gating control, the pulse delay generators driving the gating operation must possess picosecond - level delay precision.This paper presents the design and implementation of a high - precision, low - jitter pulse delay generator. The proposed hybrid delay architecture addresses the limitations of single - delay solutions in balancing precision and range: a coarse delay with a 5 ns step is implemented using a Field - Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), while a fine delay step of 10.07 ps is achieved with a dedicated delay chip. This design provides an effective technical approach for developing low - cost, high - performance timing control systems in astronomical instrumentation and offers a key electronic solution for advancing high - time - resolution astronomical devices.

Items.Authors: Qihang Zhang, Yi Wu, Shuangquan Chen, Yonggang Gu, Chao Zhai
Items.Title: Design of the positioning robot's sensorless closed-loop drive system for LAMOST
Items.Abstract: LAMOST is currently undergoing renovation. To further enhance observational efficiency, a novel integrated fiber positioning robot has been designed, driven by a 4mm miniature hollow cup motor to control three times the number of fibers within the same space. Most such miniature motors employ open-loop control. To further improve positioning accuracy and controllability, we propose a closed-loop control scheme based on sensorless position sensing. This paper details the design of the fiber positioning robot's drive system, focusing on its software and hardware components. It covers communication protocols, closed-loop algorithms, and mechanical structures. Testing was conducted on a pilot platform with visual feedback to validate fiber positioning accuracy. Experimental results confirm that this drive system achieves significantly improved positioning accuracy compared to open-loop control, providing a more efficient and precise control solution for fiber positioning.

Items.Authors: Romain J. L. Fétick, Cyril Petit, Thierry Fusco, Nicolas Vedrenne, Jean Francois Sauvage, Pierre Louis Mayeur
Items.Title: Design of the PROVIDENCE adaptive optics system
Items.Abstract: The PROVIDENCE station will be a 2.5-meter telescope installed in Observatoire de Haute Provence (France) by early 2029. It is designed for both astronomical and Low-Earth Orbit satellites imaging. The first light instrument will be a visible imager, coupled to an infrared adapted optics system. The SSA case is challenging since operations must be performed on faint sources, extended objects, at low elevation, and at fast apparent speed. We explore the possibility to perform AO in such cases with a pyramid wavefront sensor, that is highly sensitive but suffers from non-linearities. A Gain Scheduling Camera is envisaged in order to compensate in real time the effect of the optical gains in the AO loop. End-to-end simulations are performed in order to demonstrate the possibility to run the PROVIDENCE AO system in harsh conditions. Fine management of the pyramid WFS non linearities should also be coupled to predictive control for mitigation of the temporal error.

Items.Authors: Pornapa Artsang, Amayas Renaï, Pakakaew Rittipruk, Pongphol Suchirapatpong
Items.Title: Design the auto-guiding system of the solar tracker to improve pointing precision and long-term stability for fiber-fed solar spectroscopy
Items.Abstract: We describe the development of an auto-guiding system for a two-axis solar tracker intended for Sun-as-a-star, fiber-fed spectroscopic observations. Real-time monitoring of the solar disk position is performed using a guide sensor, and closed-loop control algorithms are implemented to apply pointing corrections in altitude and azimuth. Guiding performance is characterized through measurements of tracking accuracy, stability, and repeatability over long observing sequences, with particular attention to illumination stability at the fiber input. The system demonstrates that reliable solar auto-guiding can be achieved with a compact, mechanically simple tracker, offering a cost-effective solution for long-term spectroscopic monitoring.

Items.Authors: Nicholas MacDonald, Jean-Thomas Landry, Marc-Andre Boucher, William Deich, Daren Dillon, Michael Gonzales, Renata Kupke, Dale Sandford, Andy Skemer, Deno Stelter
Items.Title: Design, fabrication, and testing of the SCALES dispersion carousel and optical mounts
Items.Abstract: The SCALES instrument, planned for deployment in 2026 on the Keck II telescope, employs a 14-position carousel to position dispersive elements at the spectrograph pupil. Operating over the 2–5 µm wavelength range, SCALES provides multiple spectral passbands and resolutions for high-contrast integral-field spectroscopy. This paper describes the design of the disperser carousel, including its mechanism architecture, optical interfaces, and associated opto-mechanical components. We present the assembly and integration approach, followed by performance measurements obtained under both ambient laboratory conditions and the instrument’s cryogenic operating temperature of 100 K.

Items.Authors: Lison Malo, Francois Wildi, Philippe Vallée, Jonathan Saint-Antoine, Sébastien Bovay, Francois Bouchy, Bachar Wehbe, Alexandre Cabral, Michael Sordet, Frédérique Baron, René Doyon, Gaspare Lo Curto, Nuno Santos
Items.Title: Design, performances, and upgrade of the thermal enclosure for the NIRPS Cryogenic spectrograph at La Silla Observatory
Items.Abstract: NIRPS is a nIR, AO-assisted, high-resolution spectrograph installed on the ESO 3.6m telescope at LaSilla Observatory. Operating at 75 K, the cryogenic instrument features a fiber-fed, cross-dispersed R4 echelle design, providing simultaneous coverage of the 0.97–1.85 μm at a resolution of 80,000. In May 2023, a thermal enclosure was implemented to achieve long-term temperature stability within ±3 mK over 30 days. The enclosure was designed to be cost-effective while ensuring accessibility for preventive maintenance. However, seasonal temperature variations in the Coudé room were so significant that they required a substantial increase in the power dissipated inside the enclosure. The first upgrade, integrated an external power supply regulated by a Lakeshore 336 controller. Additionally, fans and heat exhaust components were installed to mitigate heat accumulation inside the thermal enclosure during vacuum pump operation, reducing downtime and improving overall thermal performance.

Items.Authors: Rafael Alves de Souza Ribeiro, Carlos Eduardo Fermino, Tommy Lazaneo Zirnberger, Decio de Moura Rinaldi, Tiago Giorgetti, Daiana Ribeiro Bortoletto, José Octavio Armani Paschoal, Cláudia Lúcia Mendes de Oliveira
Items.Title: Design, prototyping, and qualification of large-aperture optical shutters for astronomical instruments
Items.Abstract: The Prof. João Steiner Institute for Instrumentation and Data Science (Steiner Institute) has launched a program to develop and fabricate scientific-grade optical shutters, enhancing the diversification and resilience of the global astronomical instrumentation supply chain. The initiative is based on a formal technology transfer agreement between Bonn-Shutter GmbH i. L. and the Steiner Institute, and is carried out through the Institute's subsidiaries, which will produce the resulting systems. Initial activities include revisiting product families, establishing mechanical and electronic design standards, updating qualification workflows for wide-aperture shutters used in imaging and spectroscopic instruments, and enhancing long-term service capabilities. This paper discusses the program’s motivation and initial technical progress, and outlines the role the Steiner Institute aims to play as a reliable, technically compatible source of shutter solutions for the astronomical community.

Items.Authors: Gerardo Capobianco, Giorgio Bergamin, Alessandro Bemporad, Stefania Rasetti
Items.Title: Development and calibration of a geomagnetic disturbance measurement station
Items.Abstract: During a geomagnetic storm, as first observed by Carrington in 1859, significant electric currents are induced in the ionosphere and magnetosphere, resulting in a disturbance of the Earth’s geomagnetic field. Monitoring the Earth’s geomagnetic field is a highly effective way to track solar activity. These measurements are currently acquired in Italy by a limited network of stations managed by the INGV (National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology), located in Castello Tesino (TN), L'Aquila (AQ), Duronia (CB), and Lampedusa (AG). In the framework of SWELTO – Space WEather Laboratory in Turin Observatory, a new geomagnetic disturbance measurement station has been successfully installed and is operational at the Astrophysical Observatory of Turin since the end of 2024. This paper will detail the requirements, development, and calibration of the new station, alongside a presentation of the first measurements recorded during geomagnetic storms.

Items.Authors: Hiroshi Akitaya, Tomoki Morokuma, Koji S. Kawabata
Items.Title: Development and commissioning of the near-ultraviolet imager SCUID for the 1.5m Kanata telescope
Items.Abstract: We developed a near-ultraviolet (NUV) imager SCUID, which is capable of efficient imaging at the NUV wavelength with a field-of-view of 5 arcmin by 5 arcmin, for the 1.5m Kanata telescope at Higashi-Hiroshima Observatory in Hiroshima, Japan. The optical components and detector were carefully selected to maximize the instrument's throughput in this wavelength range. We achieve a 5-sigma detection limit of 18–19 AB mag in the u-band with a 100-sec exposure, as reported in the last conference. Recently, we have installed an instrument selector unit and a rotatable filter wheel at the Kanata Nasmyth focus, enabling remote operation of the instrument. The linear polarimetry module, which consists of a wiregrid polarizer and a rotatable half-wave plate, has been designed and will be installed in the instrument.

Items.Authors: Fabien Grisé, Brian Fleming, Nicholas Kruczek, Emily Farr, Briana Indahl, Kevin France, Jake McCoy, Randall McEntaffer, Kristina Davis
Items.Title: Development and fabrication of an EUV, ultra-low blaze angle diffraction grating for a NASA space telescope
Items.Abstract: The EUV spectral range holds critical information about million-degree  plasmas in hot white dwarf atmospheres, accretion processes, and the  interstellar medium. EUV radiation also drives atmospheric escape from  planets, making its characterization essential for assessing exoplanet  habitability around active host stars. Despite its scientific  importance, the EUV band has remained largely unexplored since NASA's  Extreme Ultraviolet Explorer (EUVE) mission that operated throughout  the 1990s, primarily due to severe interstellar extinction.  Recent advances in nanofabrication now enable a new generation of  high-efficiency diffraction gratings optimized for EUV wavelengths. We  present the design, fabrication, and characterization of an ultra-low  blaze angle diffraction grating developed for NASA's MANTIS CubeSat  mission. Our prototype testing results demonstrate  performance advances that address key technology gaps identified by  NASA and support future flagship missions including HWO.

Items.Authors: Ricardo Parra
Items.Title: Development and implementation of sustainable, large scale, industrial stripping and silver coating processes for ESO’s ELT M1
Items.Abstract: The ESO’s ELT M1 requires continuous coating renovation of 798 Zerodur segments throughout operations. This review paper presents the industrial stripping and protected silver coating processes developed to support high-volume, long-term segment maintenance. At the time of this submission, 274 segments have been coated and integrated, demonstrating process maturity and operational readiness. In addition to the process description, the paper will present statistical results from the coating of more than 300 production units, including variability across them, and long-term ageing results from qualification samples exposed and monitored for up to ten years.  The stripping process is based on a selective cerium sulfate and sulfuric acid formulation established through thermodynamic modelling and repeated exposure tests on Zerodur®. The solution removes the complete protected silver stack without measurable roughness growth across cycles and produces a stable near-surface chemistry.

Items.Authors: Laura Proserpio, Giorgia Sironi, Giovanni Pareschi, Gianpiero Tagliaferri, Michele Buzzi, Rachele Millul, Luigi Lessio, Nicola La Palombara, Salvatore Scuderi, Alessio Trois, Alida Marchetti, Carla Andreoni, Anna Maria Torricelli, Giuseppe Valsecchi, Matteo Redaelli, Fabio Zocchi, Alessandro Zanoni
Items.Title: Development and large production of the large (1.8 m) aspheric secondary mirrors for the Schwarzschild-Couder telescopes for the ASTRI and SST/CTAO air Cherenkov array via hot slumping replication
Items.Abstract: The dual-mirror aplanatic Schwarzschild–Couder (SC) design for 4 m class telescopes in the ASTRI Mini-Array and CTAO requires large, highly aspheric secondary mirrors with moderate figure and coating performance. To support over 40 SC telescopes, an industrially scalable hot-slumping process was developed to produce 1.8-meter-diameter aspheric secondaries. This includes precision mandrels, high-temperature slumpings of 20 mm float-glass, and 3D mapping metrology. The mandrel was upgraded from steel to cast iron for better accuracy and process stability. Post-slumping involves gluing mechanical pads and applying reflective coatings optimized for Cherenkov wavelengths. The results confirm that the technique meets the surface and slope error tolerances with high reproducibility. Successful fabrication of these 1.8-m monolithic secondary mirrors is a significant milestone, supporting next-gen gamma-ray astronomy, and possibly also advancing optical telescope mirror production.

Items.Authors: Phillip Wise, Stephen Bongiorno
Items.Title: Development and testing of a circular whiffle tree fixture for characterizing full-shell X-ray optics
Items.Abstract: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC) produces full shell replicated x-ray optics. It is desirable to test the performance of these shells at their natural shape so that their production, handling, and preparation for flight can be refined. The method of testing requires the shells be positioned horizontally such that they experience measurable deformation due to gravity. Various mounting methods are utilized to negate the figure change caused by this deformation, but they have issues with repeatability and setup time. An alternative mounting solution utilizes a circular whiffle-tree to apply radially dependent force on the exterior of the shell to minimize deformation. The circular whiffle is advantageous in that it allows for quick mounting of shells, may reduce gravity deformation, and is relatively low cost. This presentation covers the design, manufacture, and testing of the circular wiffle against the mounting method currently used in MSFC’s 100-meter x-ray beamline.

Items.Authors: Fabio D'Anca, Alfonso Collura, Javier Pérez-Álvarez, Marco Barbera, Andrea Bocchieri, Pasquale Bonfà, Daniele Brienza, Anna Brucalassi, Vincenzo Davide Cardinale, Paolo Chioetto, Gaspare Di Cicca, Ugo Lo Cicero, Alejandro Fernández-Soler, Maurizio Filizzolo, Manuele Gangi, Alberto Gulizzi, Elisa Guerriero, Riccardo Lilli, Giuseppe Malaguti, Pierfilippo Mazzasette, Andrea Meduri, Angelo Olivieri, Emanuele Pace, Enzo Pascale, Paolo Picchi, Gianpaolo Preti, Claudio Saitta, Antonio Scippa, Luisa Sciortino, Michela Todaro, Elisabetta Tommasi, Salvatore Varisco, Andrea Tozzi, Dervis Vernani, Paola Zuppella, Riccardo Claudi, Giuseppina Micela
Items.Title: Development of a cryogenic test facility for Ariel’s primary mirror
Items.Abstract: The INAF Astronomical Observatory of Palermo has adapted the XACT facility to perform cryogenic testing of the 1-meter primary mirror for ESA’s Ariel mission, which operates at about 55 K. Thermoelastic effects at this temperature require a cryogenic interferometric campaign to recover the WFE and evaluate optical behavior in a representative environment. The facility includes a 2 m × 2 m vacuum chamber with a 1.4 m entrance hatch, a closed-loop helium cryocooler reaching 30 K, and an optical setup based on a 4D interferometer, a hexapod, and a vacuum optical window. The mirror is supported by an isostatic multi-DoF fork mount, with cooling provided through copper plates, heat shields, and thermal straps linked by an aluminum structure. Simulations show thermal gradients below 5 K and mirror temperatures below the required 90 K. The paper presents the setup, test activities, preliminary interferometric results, and related critical issues.

Items.Authors: Raphaël Pourcelot, Markus Feldt, Thomas Bertram, Peter Bizenberger, Markus Kasper, Stefan Ströbele, Silvia Scheithauer
Items.Title: Development of an adaptive optics testbed at MPIA for the ELT/Planetary Camera and Spectrograph (PCS)
Items.Abstract: The Planetary Camera and Spectrograph (PCS) is a proposed second-generation instrument for the European Southern Observatory (ESO) Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) aimed at direct exoplanet imaging, requiring extreme adaptive optics (AO). Building on experience from ELT/METIS as well as VLT/SPHERE adaptive optics and its upgrade SAXO+, MPIA is initiating a modular testbed to advance key AO technologies.    It will integrate two deformable mirrors, including a high-density deformable mirror prototype developed by Bertin-ALPAO in collaboration with ESO. The testbed will enable the evaluation of Fourier filtering wavefront sensors, novel mask designs, and control architectures (woofer-tweeter or independent AO stages). MPIA’s real-time control expertise enables testing of predictive and machine learning-enhanced AO strategies. In this work we present MPIA’s testbed development status and the design choices to push the extreme AO technologies for future ELT instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Jongyeob Park, Sujin Kim, Jeong-Yeol Han, Eunsu Park, Hojin Lee, Kyung-Suk Cho
Items.Title: Development of an EUV imager for the Sun–Earth L4 mission
Items.Abstract: Sun–Earth L4 observations provide a complementary 60° offset viewpoint that expands solar coverage, improves 3D characterization of coronal structures and eruptions, and enhances the overall accuracy and continuity of space weather monitoring. An EUV Imager on the L4 mission will enable global coronal monitoring, offering critical data for understanding solar eruptions and mitigating space weather impacts. Korea has established core technologies for EUV instrumentation, including precision optics, multilayer coatings, and thin-film metal filters. In addition, synchrotron-based calibration facilities have been developed to validate instrument performance across EUV wavelengths, positioning Korea with the infrastructure necessary for next-generation space observatories. This presentation will outline the scientific significance of an EUV Imager in the L4 mission, review Korea’s current technological capabilities, and present development strategies for future EUV instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Michael Sigwarth, Hemanth Pruthvi, Falk Hoffmann, Markus Roth, Falk Eilenberger, Reinhard Geiß, Stefan Schwinde, Sascha Ehrhardt, Peter Munzert
Items.Title: Development of large lithium niobate wafer for Fabry-Pérot interferometer
Items.Abstract: For a solar full-disc imaging spectrometer with a 200-mm clear aperture solar telescope, a lithium niobate (LiNbO₃) crystal-based Fabry–Pérot interferometer with a clear aperture of 100 to 120 mm would be required. Such a wafer, polished and coated to the required specifications, has never been manufactured. Meanwhile, LiNbO₃ has become available in sizes up to eight inches, mainly for optoelectronic applications.   We present results from our initial assessment of preparing a commercial 4-inch-diameter, 250-µm-thick, Z-cut LiNbO₃ wafer for optical applications, including polishing and coating.

Items.Authors: Pablo Jiménez, Cristóbal Padilla, Jorge Jiménez
Items.Title: Development of setups for the characterisation of Novel p-on-n VLWIR Detectors
Items.Abstract: As part of the CHIPS-JU ATHENA program, new p-on-n VLWIR devices have been developed by CEA-Leti and Lynred with extended cut-off wavelengths up to 15 µm and improved operability at elevated operating temperatures. We present the commissioning and validation strategy implemented at IFAE for the experimental setups designed to support these next-generation technologies. We outline the requirements and implementation of the dedicated cryogenic and optical systems, capable of delivering controlled broadband illumination across the 0.8–15 µm range, and describe the procedures defined to verify their performance, stability, and operational readiness. Commissioning results will be presented, and a set of preliminary detector tests will be carried out to validate the performance of the setups. These activities will confirm that the systems meet the required functional specifications and are fully prepared for upcoming experimental campaigns within the ATHENA detector program.

Items.Authors: Alexander S. Kutyrev, Paul Scowen, Meng-Ping Chang, Kywoon Kim, Ming Ke, Nick Costen, Ron Hu, Eduardo Aguayo, Fred Wang, Edward Wollack, Timothy Miller, Allison Youngblood, Stephan McCandliss, Mackenzie Carlson, Emily Witt
Items.Title: Development of the next-generation microshutter arrays for the UV/visible spectroscopy
Items.Abstract: Next-generation microshutter arrays (MSA) technology is under active development to meet the demanding multiplexing and target-selection requirements of the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). These next generation devices feature significantly larger formats compare to the previous JWST version, enhanced actuation efficiency, and improved robustness. Large-format next-generation microshutter arrays are currently in fabrication, with parallel progress on the accompanying system-level test hardware, including the vacuum chamber and the accompanying drive electronics.   In addition to the HWO development effort, small-format versions of the next-generation microshutter arrays have already demonstrated successful flight performance in the OAx-FORTIS suborbital program. A new version of the small MSA will be delivered to the next OAx-FORTIS flight, providing continued validation of the technology and a rapid path for maturing design features relevant to the large HWO-type arrays.

Items.Authors: Krittapas Chanchaiworawit, Jitsupa Paenoi, Samattachai Tanun, Teerawat Kuha, Auychai Laoyang, That Chomchuen, Pakawat Prasit, Thansita Thomrungpiyathan, Pathompong Butpan, Rungrit Anutarawiramkul, Anuphong Inpan, Suchinno Kanthum, Manlika Pinkaew, Apichat Leckngam, Kantapong Tharawan
Items.Title: Development of upgraded mechanical components for the low-resolution spectrograph (lrs) and the compact low-resolution spectrograph (colors)
Items.Abstract: We present the development of upgraded mechanical components that enhance the operational efficiency of the Low-Resolution Spectrograph (LRS) at the 2.4-m Thai National Telescope and the Compact Low-Resolution Spectrograph (CoLoRS) at the Thai Robotic Telescopes network. Key processes include installation, commissioning, verification, and on-sky operation. The LRS incorporates an ANDOR Newton 940 CCD with a new liquid-cooling system that reaches −100 °C at 60% power and maintains stable performance for 10 hours, representing a 16.8% improvement. An adjustable stage for the ZWO ASI 6200MM guiding camera enables precise focusing. For CoLoRS, a lightweight adapter with an integrated guiding shaft allows rapid installation, while FEA confirms displacement below 0.01 mm. A redesigned counterweight system improves compactness and cable management.

Items.Authors: Myung K. Cho, Hong-Suh Yim, Jaemann Kyeong, Gary Poczulp, Jung Hyun Jo, Myung-Jin Kim, Ming Liang, Ellie Hileman, Sungki Cho
Items.Title: Development of Wide Field sky survey telescopes
Items.Abstract: We present a summary of the design and development for Near Space Optical Survey telescopes. This is a collaborative effort between the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute (KASI) and the NSF’s National Optical-Infrared Astronomy Research Laboratory (NOIRLab) aiming to discover and catalog near-Earth asteroids. This sky survey optical telescope is a 1.6m primary mirror with a 5 square degree field of view, and will be installed and operated at the Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory (CTIO) in Chile. It will have a wide field corrector unit in a prime focus configuration with a set of 7 corrector lenses. The telescope design at an equatorial mount was adopted and enhanced based on the features from current Korea Microlensing Telescope Network at CTIO. This sky survey telescope will be the first dedicated observation facility for asteroid survey in the southern hemisphere in 1.6-meter class telescopes. The key optical and mechanical systems in telescope will be addressed.

Items.Authors: Tianrui Sun, Yiding Ping, Fan Li
Items.Title: development progress and science drivers of the 4.2m ground-based astrometric telescope
Items.Abstract: Purple Mountain Observatory is building a new 4.2-meter telescope at the Lenghu B+ site in Qinghai Province, China. The 4.2-m ground-based astrometric telescope is intended to carry out follow-up observations of gamma-ray bursts and gravitational-wave events, obtain spectra of supernovae, and perform astrometric measurements of selected Solar System targets.  The telescope has one Cassegrain focus and two Nasmyth foci. The Cassegrain focus hosts the main imaging camera, which includes multiple filters and provides a field of view of approximately 10′ × 10′. The two Nasmyth ports will be equipped with a medium- to low-resolution spectrograph and an adaptive-optics camera.  This presentation will report on the development progress of the telescope and describe the range of scientific programs it is designed to support.

Items.Authors: Zibo Jiang, Kunxing Chen, Xuefei Gong, Lijun Wu, Junxue Wang, Xiaoqin Yan, Songxin Dai
Items.Title: Development progress of discrete symmetric  stressed mirror polishing fixture
Items.Abstract: At present Many ground-based astronomical telescopes adopt a spliced mirror form for their primary mirrors.The stressed mirror annular polishing technology has the advantages of high processing efficiency and smooth surface shape, and is suitable for polishing batch spliced segments. In this article a new symmetrical loading device scheme based on bidirectional cylinders for annular polishing processing is proposed, benefiting from previous experience in stressed mirror annular polishing. First a method for implementing loading pressure control based on RS485-wireless transmission is provided. Then the distribution of loading forces were obtained by calculation. Finally the deformation distribution of the loading rods and carbon fiber composite substrate were obtained by simulation of Finite Element Analysis. This loading device can also be conveniently used for stressed mirror grinding and polishing based on a classical single axis polishing machine.

Items.Authors: Takafumi Kamizuka, Yuki Hirao, Akira C. Naruse, Takashi Miyata, Shigeyuki Sako, Itsuki Sakon, Kengo Tachibana, Riko Senoo, Yuki Kojima, Ichiro Jikuya, Noboru Ebizuka, Takuya Hosobata, Sunao Hasegawa, Fumihiko Usui, Ryou Ohsawa, Mizuho Uchiyama, Takashi Onaka, Hirokazu Kataza, Kotaro Kohno, Kentaro Motohara, Takeo Minezaki, Fumi Egusa, Masahiro Konishi, Hidenori Takahashi, Kazuya Matsubayashi, Hiroaki Sameshima, Kana Morokuma-Matsui, Mitsuyoshi Yamagishi, Masataka Imai, Takashi Horiuchi, Natsuko Kato, Yuzuru Yoshii
Items.Title: Development status of TAO/MIMIZUKU: performance of the long-wavelength MIR (MIR-L) channel and NIR channel upgrades
Items.Abstract: MIMIZUKU is the first-generation mid-infrared instrument for the University of Tokyo Atacama Observatory (TAO) 6.5-m telescope. TAO provides high atmospheric transmittance in the infrared including unique access to the 30-micron band (30-40 microns). MIMIZUKU covers 1.2-38 microns for imaging and low-resolution spectroscopy and enables long-term monitoring by achieving accurate atmospheric absorption correction using its Field Stacker system.  MIMIZUKU has three optical channels: NIR (1.2–5.6 microns), MIR-S (7.0–26 microns), and MIR-L (24–38 microns). Recent development has focused on the NIR and MIR-L channels. The NIR channel was upgraded with a reflective slit and grism to enhance throughput and field of view. The MIR-L channel was fully integrated and tested, incorporating a 128x128 Si:Sb array, a silicon moth-eye lens, membrane metal-mesh filters, and a cryogenic optical-path switch. We report the latest status and expected on-sky performance at TAO.
